title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
interviewTips: Clarify if low_fats and recyclable can be NULL or lowercase y, and whether to return only product_id or full rows.
Trade-off: row-by-row loop is easy to understand but slow in pandas, declarative WHERE and vectorized mask lets the engine optimize filtering.
Edge-case tip: handle empty table, zero matches, and ensure case-sensitive comparison to 'Y' not truthy values.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Row Scan
approaches.intuition: Check every product one by one and keep it only if low_fats is Y and recyclable is Y, like manually scanning the table.
approaches.theory: This is relational selection sigma with predicate low_fats='Y' AND recyclable='Y'. Scanning all n rows and testing the predicate is O(n). It is correct because AND requires both conditions true, all other combinations are rejected.

timeComplexity.explanation: Visit each of n products once and do O(1) comparison. In pandas iterrows adds high constant overhead.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Store k matching product_ids where k <= n, plus O(1) extra for loop variables.

edgeCases: no Y,Y rows returns empty result
all rows match returns all ids

approaches.name: Approach 2: Declarative Filter (WHERE / Vectorized)
approaches.intuition: Let the engine filter for you: SQL WHERE with AND or pandas boolean mask or STL and Stream filter, no manual per-row branching in user code.
approaches.theory: Same selection sigma but executed declaratively. SQL optimizer can use indexes, pandas uses vectorized C-level loops, C++ copy_if and Java Stream express predicate as lambda. Logic: keep row iff low_fats='Y' AND recyclable='Y', project only product_id.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass over n rows by engine. Same asymptotic as brute force but much smaller constant via vectorized C loop and SQL optimization.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only output of k matching ids plus temporary boolean mask of size n in pandas which is O(n) auxiliary but reclaimed.

edgeCases: NULL values never equal Y so correctly excluded
lowercase y not matched due to case-sensitive compare
